en: The Dhāraṇī and Hymn named Vasudhārā: Om! Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble and Glorious Vasudhārā!
She who possesses a divine form, a beautiful form, and a gentle form, the bestower of strength.
She is the upholder of wealth, the sustainer of the earth, the glory of riches, the bestower of prosperity, and the most excellent.
The Earth, the Upholder, the Sustainer, the Refuge, she who is affectionate toward her devotees;
the Goddess Prajñāpāramitā, Wisdom, the Increaser of Fortune and Intelligence. (2)
She is the Vidyādharī, the Auspicious One, the Subtle, the Teacher, and the Mother (Mātṛkā) everywhere;
she is the Youthful Goddess, the Savior, and the Sovereign of the Lords of the Bestowal of Knowledge.
Adorned and the mother of beings, she is decorated with all ornaments;
she terrifies the difficult-to-tame, and being formidable, she is fierce with fierce prowess.
The goddess Dānapāramitā is the bestower of rain, possessing a divine form;
she is the treasury of all auspiciousness, renown, fortune, glory, and virtue. (5)
Dahanī, Mālinī, Caṇḍī, Śabarī, Sarvamātrikā, Kṛtāntaśāsanī, Raudrī, Kaumārī, and Viśvarūpiṇī. || 6 ||
The goddess Vīryapāramitā brings joy to the world;
she is an ascetic of fierce form, bestowing supernatural power, accomplishment, and strength. (7)
Blessed, meritorious, and highly fortunate, she is unconquered and possesses victorious prowess;
she is the singular benefit for the world, a science that delivers one in battle and is auspicious.
The goddess Kṣāntipāramitā is virtuous and meditative;
she is Padminī, the bearer of a lotus, the lover of the lotus, and the one seated upon a lotus throne.
Pure in form, of great splendor, golden-hued, and radiant;
the Great Goddess Cintāmaṇi, who holds the book of wisdom.
She is the treasure ascended upon the peak, the beloved wealth of the house of merit;
she is the great primordial state of the three realms, adorned with divine ornaments.
The Mother of all Buddhas, the Sovereign Lady of the Jewel Realm,
is the Goddess to be meditated upon as emptiness, free from both existence and non-existence. (12)
O Vaineya, why was [this] not placed [upon you]—it which cuts through divine afflictions, shatters all Māras, and agitates the seven netherworlds? (13)
She is Brahmāṇī, the Mother of the Vedas, the Secret One, and the Dweller in the Secret;
she is Sarasvatī, the Large-eyed One, who dwells in the four sublime states of a Brahmin. || 14 ||
The Tathāgata’s [consort], most delightful, the Vajra-holder, the upholder of the Dharma;
the sovereign of the realm of action, the Vidyā, whose mandala is a mass of universal flames. (15)
She is the awakening for all sentient beings, crowned with the factors of enlightenment;
she is meditative concentration, wisdom endowed with liberation, and she manifests both non-duality and duality. || 16 ||
She accomplishes all aims, auspicious, possessing immeasurable prowess in the form of a woman;
she reveals the paths of the Buddhas and shows the way to those who have lost their path. (17)
Vāgīśvarī, the Great Peace, the Protector, the Sustainer, the Bestower of Wealth;
she who assumes a female form, the Perfected One, the Yoginī, and the Sovereign of Yoga-born beings. (18)
She is the captivator of the mind, the great stride, she whose appearance is dear due to her good fortune;
she possesses the compassionate gaze of a caravan leader and has the nature of all Tathāgatas. (19)
Salutations to you, O Great Goddess, bestower of the welfare of all sentient beings;
salutations to you of divine form, Vasudhārā—homage be to you!
The man who recites these one hundred and eight names at the three times of day will certainly attain perfection and the fulfillment of his desired aims and aspirations. (21)
Whatever extremely grave sin has been committed through ignorance, all of that is swiftly destroyed by the mere recollection of Sarvabhadra. (22)
Alternatively, one endowed with moral discipline shall remember seven past births;
he shall be beloved, his words shall be accepted, and he shall be handsome and pleasing to behold. (23)
He is born as one worthy of offerings among families of Brahmins and Kṣatriyas;
finally, having attained the status of a lord of the earth, he subsequently reaches Sukhāvatī. || 24 ||
The praise of the dhāraṇī named Śrīvasudhārā,
spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One, is completed.
